learning_outcomes.text: Analyze combustion processes in energy and industrial systems, applying the principles of thermochemistry, heat transfer, and fluid mechanics to characterize the behavior of premixed and diffusion flames.

syllabus_topics: Approach to the study of combustion
Heat of reaction and calorific value of a fuel
Premixed flame emissions: NOx, CO, HC
teaching_methods: Expository class (participative lecture, conferences, company visits, trade fair attendance, etc.)
Participative class (individual or group problem solving, role-playing, technique application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.)
Laboratory activities (research sessions on classroom didactics)
Integrated project (planning, design, and execution of activities to solve a problem or address a task)
Tutoring (personalized and small group attention, review, reorientation of class materials, learning, and work completion)
Group work (preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects, etc. for submission and presentation in practical classes)
Individual study (preparation of readings, exams, exercises, class preparation, etc.)
assessment_rules: Written tests must be passed with a grade higher than 4. The course will be considered passed if the final grade is equal to or greater than 5 points and none of the grades for the written parts are below 4 points. In the first call, the failed part or parts can be retaken. In the second call, Project grades will be maintained. For students exempt from the Integrated Project (PI), its weight will be added to the written tests.
